items.text: Is your house at its tidiest when you've got a deadline coming up?

level1.label: 时间状语从句
level1.text: when you've got a deadline coming up

items.text: Do you have a list of jobs that you really need to do, but you really don't want to start doing?

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: a list of jobs that you really need to do, but you really don't want to start doing

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: that you really need to do, but you really don't want to start doing

items.text: Procrastination can mean that we spend more time putting off a job than we'd ever actually spend completing it.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that we spend more time putting off a job than we'd ever actually spend completing it

items.text: Understanding why we do it might help us to understand how to stop doing it.

level1.label: 宾语补足语
level1.text: to understand how to stop doing it

items.text: There are different reasons why people procrastinate.
Some people avoid tasks if they can relate them to traumatic situations in their past.

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: if they can relate them to traumatic situations in their past

items.text: Sometimes we don't do certain tasks because we're swamped with other things.

level1.label: 原因状语从句
level1.text: because we're swamped with other things

items.text: If people are unhappy about being asked to do something, they might put it off to feel like they are regaining some control.

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: If people are unhappy about being asked to do something

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: to feel like they are regaining some control

level2.label: 宾语从句
level2.text: like they are regaining some control

items.text: Another common reason for procrastination is just the worry that doing something will be unpleasant or that we will not be able to do it well enough to satisfy ourselves.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: just the worry that doing something will be unpleasant or that we will not be able to do it well enough to satisfy ourselves

level2.label: 同位语从句
level2.text: that doing something will be unpleasant or that we will not be able to do it well enough to satisfy ourselves

items.text: This last kind of procrastination can be a result of our mindset.
People with a perfectionist mindset are likely to have a very rigid idea of what success in a task looks like.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: likely to have a very rigid idea of what success in a task looks like

level2.label: 宾语从句
level2.text: what success in a task looks like

items.text: This is coupled with being anxious not to fail at that task.
Psychology lecturer Annemiecke Apergis-Schoute points out that procrastination can be the result of a struggle between our brain's reward and threat systems.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that procrastination can be the result of a struggle between our brain's reward and threat systems

items.text: If the threat of failure or discomfort is greater than the potential reward from doing the task, we're likely to avoid it.

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: If the threat of failure or discomfort is greater than the potential reward from doing the task

items.text: Cognitive flexibility could help us to avoid procrastinating.
If we change the way that we think about a task, it can be easier to start working on it.

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: If we change the way that we think about a task

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: easier to start working on it

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: that we think about a task

items.text: If we can challenge our expectation of what succeeding could be, and how uncomfortable working on the task will be, it can seem less threatening.

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: If we can challenge our expectation of what succeeding could be, and how uncomfortable working on the task will be

items.text: Breaking down tasks into small components also makes them less daunting as well as providing a feeling of achievement when each of these steps is completed.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: Breaking down tasks into small components

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: as well as providing a feeling of achievement when each of these steps is completed

level2.label: 时间状语从句
level2.text: when each of these steps is completed

items.text: It can also be useful to consider what triggers procrastination for you.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: useful to consider what triggers procrastination for you

items.text: Having a better understanding of this can help you get things done.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: Having a better understanding of this
